chunks: "The best of you are your generous ones, and the worst of you are your stingy ones. And from pure iman is righteousness toward brothers and striving in their needs. Indeed, the one who is righteous toward the brothers is surely loved by the Most Merciful, and in that is humiliation for Satan, distancing from the fires, and entry into the gardens."

Then he said to Jamil: "O Jamil, inform the choicest of your companions of this." I said: "May I be made your ransom, who are the choicest of my companions?" He said: "They are those who are righteous toward the brothers in hardship and ease."

Then he said: "O Jamil, indeed the possessor of much finds that easy upon him, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has praised in that the possessor of little. So He said in His Book: 'And they prefer others over themselves even though there is privation with them; and whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, then those are the successful ones.'"

key_terms.النِّيرَانِ: the fires; the fires of Hell
key_terms.الْبِرُّ بِالْإِخْوَانِ: righteousness toward brothers; doing good to fellow believers
key_terms.بُخَلَاؤُكُمْ: your stingy ones; those characterized by miserliness
key_terms.حَوَائِجِهِمْ: their needs; the matters and necessities requiring assistance
key_terms.خَالِصِ الْإِيمَانِ: pure iman; sincere and unalloyed faith
key_terms.خَصَاصَةٌ: privation; a state of need and scarcity
key_terms.سُمَحَاؤُكُمْ: your generous ones; those marked by openhandedness and liberality
key_terms.مَرْغَمَةُ الشَّيْطَانِ: humiliation of Satan; that which abases and frustrates him

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describe generosity and helping fellow believers as signs of true iman?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that generosity and serving the needs of fellow believers are among the clearest signs of pure iman. It presents kindness to brothers as beloved to Allah, a means of humiliating Shaytan, and a cause of salvation and entry into Paradise. It also highlights the special merit of selflessness from those who have little, echoing the Quranic praise of altruism despite personal need.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1707 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"The best among you are the generous ones, and the worst among you are the stingy ones. A sign of true faith is kindness toward brothers and striving to fulfill their needs. Indeed, the one who is kind to their brothers is loved by the Most Merciful. Such kindness humiliates Satan, distances one from the fires of Hell, and grants entrance to Paradise."

Imam (as) then said to Jamil: "O Jamil, share this with the noble of your companions."
I said: "May I be your ransom, who are the noble of my companions?"
Imam (as) replied: "They are those who are kind to their brothers in both ease and hardship."

Then Imam (as) said: "O Jamil, indeed, for the wealthy, it is easier to do this. However, Allah (swt) the Exalted has praised the one with little who gives despite their own need. Allah (swt) has said in His Book: And they give preference over themselves, even though they are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is they who will be successful' (Surah Al-Hashr 59:9)."
